name: Quest Self

name: Quest Intents
description: The person's quests as the standing view of what they are working toward, used to say what the work is for.
purpose: Make the AI work from the person's quests.
approach: Hold the quests and their intents as the view each representative acts from, and frame work with the intent behind it. The goals under an intent are of three levels, each ordered by the hub's Prioritization (Quest's arm calls the hub's and adds only Quest's rules): a solution's milestones (the hub's concept), a quest's period goals (each for a particular solution or strategy on the quest) and the day's goals, which are tasks. One to one: a period goal is a milestone of the solution it is for, linked by Quest's spec_solution_id (a goal's spec_metric_id and metric_target_value are optional, so a goal with no metric value is still a milestone); its order is its milestone's, with no ranking of its own. A goal that names no solution yet is asked about once, never given a second milestone; the day's tasks sit under the period goal they serve.

name: Feed Context Sources
description: The AI catches up on what is new in a quest since it last looked.
purpose: Help an assistant catch up on a work item where people left off, so it answers what is new and open and not what it has already seen.
approach: Collect the items added to a work item since the assistant last looked and mark which of them ask for something.
out_of_scope: Finding older background that is not new since the last look, and deciding when standing work starts (Proactivity does that) or what matters first (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. The exact set of offered items and open asks matches the stated rules on the synthetic quests, with the age and count bounds holding. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A live run once treated a habit log and a daily reflection as asks and later reported them as still owed, so channels declare whether they carry asks. A reply written after a note is not proof the note was handled, and an assistant hearing its own words echoed back wastes budget. Card-scoped channels are relevant by where they were written, while user-scoped ones need a relevance judgment.
measures_of_success: The exact set of offered items and open asks matches the stated rules on synthetic quests: own words in, assistant echoes and unattributed notes out, answered and seen items not repeated, bounds respected. Standing conditions: Keep age and count bounds holding.
parameters: A source declares a name, a one-line description, and flags for whether its items need a relevance judgment, an admission judgment, tracking as asks, or relaying onto the work item. The engine takes the sources to watch, the channels always checked, and a clock; a collect call takes the item, an optional since time and the delivered-run history.
inputs: A collect request naming the work item and the time of the last look, plus whatever the channel's client returns (notes, goal updates, decisions, and similar).
outputs: A bundle of context updates, each with an item id, its text and author, and whether it needs a response, plus the set of open asks.
effects: Advances the watermark of what has been seen and may record asks for later tracking. Sources never raise: a source that fails reports an empty result and says why.
usage_notes: Call at the start of a turn or task for a work item and render the bundle into the prompt. Add a channel by implementing the source interface and setting its flags honestly, since a wrong asks flag turns a person's diary into owed answers.

name: Cache Cards
description: A card backend outage costs the person no write.
purpose: Keep an assistant working through a card backend outage by serving the last known listing and holding failed writes for replay.
approach: Serve the last known card listing and hold every failed write for replay whenever the card backend is unreachable.
out_of_scope: Storing cards durably or choosing which store holds them (persist-cards does that), and sharing one cache between hosts, since the file cache is single-host.
milestones: 1. Outage cases passed by the file cache: 12 of 12, including a cold start during an outage and every failed write replayed. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. Outage cases passed by a cache shared across hosts, so every host serves the same listing.
knowledge: The repository never depends on a cache for correctness, and every backend failure is logged, counted and surfaced as a degraded status. A cold start during an outage is the case that separates a durable cache from a memory one. A file cache is single-host.
measures_of_success: On a card API that can go down, callers see identical behaviour, the stored listing is served on a cold start, and every failed write is replayed. Standing conditions: Keep caller-visible behaviour the same with or without a cache. Keep the outage loud. Keep the listing across restarts. Lose no failed write.
parameters: A cache is passed to the repository as an optional argument; the file cache takes a directory. The seam has no tuning parameters.
inputs: A full or delta listing with its latest update time, and failed writes as card id, card and team id.
outputs: The stored listing with its update time, or none, and the queued writes oldest first.
effects: Stores the listing and an outbox on each call; the durable cache writes files atomically and swallows its own I/O errors.
usage_notes: Choose the durable cache for any lane that must survive an outage across restarts; keep the null cache where failing loudly is wanted. Check the repository's health status to see degradation.
verdict_detail: memory_cache is exactly equal to file_cache on the metric (memory_cache 1 against file_cache 1), so file_cache stays; file_cache leads null_cache (null_cache 0.5 against file_cache 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0625, 6 of 12 cases disagree)

name: Persist Cards
description: Context cards live wherever the person needs them to.
purpose: Keeps context cards safe and retrievable wherever a person needs them to live, from a local folder to the Quest backend.
approach: Writes, reads, lists and deletes context cards in the chosen store, with no card lost and none duplicated.
out_of_scope: Deciding which cards suit a turn (context-retriever does that), serving a listing while the backend is down and replaying failed writes (cache-cards does that), and backend-specific logic in card handling.
milestones: 1. The same 14 conformance cases pass on the filesystem, embedded Qdrant and Quest API backends. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The same conformance cases pass against a Qdrant server and the dev Quest API, not only the embedded and fake backends.
knowledge: Persistence is a boundary: card logic lives in the store and a backend only stores and fetches. A listing that silently truncated at a page limit once made a backend fail the volume case. Backend errors must be loud and counted, not swallowed, and card identity is the pair of scope and id so the same id may exist privately and in a team.
measures_of_success: Every conformance case passes on every backend: round trip, overwrite, no loss at volume and across pages, no duplicate, delete including after restart, concurrent writers, change stamp and tolerance of bad input. Standing conditions: Lose no card, create no duplicate, and behave the same on every backend, including after restart, under concurrent writers and across paged listings.
parameters: Backend choice and connection (folder path; vector collection, embedder and vector size or server url; Quest base url, key, timeout and scope), plus the optional scope used for tenant isolation.
inputs: Card ids and card dictionaries for write (a card as defined in docs/explanation/context-assembly.md, What a context card is: id, name, keywords, summary and description, pinned files, typed content references, provenance, usage, scope tags and origin); ids for read, delete and exists.
outputs: Load-all returns a mapping of id to card, read returns a card or nothing, write and delete return success flags, and revision returns a change stamp used to invalidate caches.
effects: Durable writes to the chosen store (atomic files, vector points embedded at write time, or API calls), and for the API backend logged and counted errors.
usage_notes: Pick the backend by where the cards must live and inject it into the card store; every backend must pass the same conformance cases, so none is better when it conforms. Add a backend by implementing the protocol and a harness. A card's fields, its id rules and what is not a card are defined once in docs/explanation/context-assembly.md, What a context card is; docs/how-to/context-card-stores.md covers stores, mounts and copies.
verdict_detail: filesystem is exactly equal to quest_api on the metric (filesystem 1 against quest_api 1), so quest_api stays; qdrant is exactly equal to quest_api on the metric (qdrant 1 against quest_api 1), so quest_api stays

name: Receive Input Mid Run
description: A person can redirect an assistant while it works.
purpose: Lets a person change direction, pause or stop an assistant while it works, and be heard at its next decision.
approach: Holds each message a person sends during a run and delivers it once to the next decision of that same run.
out_of_scope: Ordering messages across different conversations, and choosing how a run responds to what it is told.
milestones: 1. Each message reaches its own run's next decision exactly once, with send-to-seen latency, acted-on share, stop-to-quiet time and cost per run recorded on live stream-json runs at 3, then 10, then 30 runs, cheapest model first.
knowledge: Interfaces used to hand-wire pending-input callables, so one generic, application-agnostic inbox replaced them. A running deep worker CAN be re-prompted: Claude Code's stream-json session takes a user message on stdin while a tool runs and reads it at its next step (0.4 s after that tool finished in a probe on this machine, 2026-10-19), and takes an interrupt that stops the running step and keeps the session. The one-shot subprocess runner cannot, so there a message is seen only at the next attempt boundary; the stream_json deep runner (run-deep-work) is the alternative that closes that gap. A priority flag documented to move running work to the background did not do so in the probe, so only the default priority is used.
measures_of_success: A message pushed before or during a run reaches the next planner decision once, only for its own conversation, through a real orchestrator, and the port contract holds. For a deep worker with a live session: every message is written once and only to its own run (two concurrent runs never cross), one that lands as the run finishes is delivered once or left unclaimed, none is lost (a message written but not confirmed seen comes back as unseen), and work finished before a stop or pause is kept. Measured next to those: send-to-seen latency (p50 and p90 seconds, from the push to the model receiving it), acted-on share (steer cases whose required change happened, checked deterministically), stop-to-quiet time (from the stop request to the last tool event) and cost per run (dollars the run reports). Standing conditions: Deliver every pushed message to the next decision of the planner or of the running worker, exactly once, only for its own run. Lose none silently.
parameters: No tuning parameters: the contract is three calls keyed by a conversation id (push, drain, peek). A distributed implementation chooses its own storage settings.
inputs: A conversation id and a message string on push; a conversation id on drain and peek.
outputs: Drain returns and removes the pending messages in arrival order; peek returns them without removing.
effects: Drain empties that conversation's queue. The orchestrator drains between goal-loop steps when an inbox is wired.
usage_notes: Push once per incoming message from whatever interface receives it and wire the same inbox into the orchestrator. Supply a shared implementation when several processes serve one conversation.

name: Replay Known Operations
description: A request that worked before is answered without planning again.
purpose: Speeds up a quest's repeated operations by recognising a request that worked before and replaying the known steps.

milestones: 1. Recipe replay and the planner-only path reach the same pass rate on repeat requests when both run live through the claude CLI, with recipe replay making fewer model calls and its hit rate recorded.
knowledge: A lookalike request must never trigger a write, so replay carries a guard for mutating operations and a minimum match score. The offline arm uses a rule model written with the cases in view, so it proves the engine, not a real model's judgment. Recipes are learned only from successes.

parameters: The recipe store path (or none for memory only), the minimum match score, scope tags for learning and matching, and the planner model tier.
inputs: A user request and the registry of available tools.
outputs: The reply text and exit reason of the run, with the tool executed and its arguments when a recipe fired.
effects: Learns a new recipe after a successful operation and rewrites the recipe file atomically under a lock; may execute a tool.
usage_notes: Enable by configuring a recipe store on the orchestrator; compare against a planner-only run on the same tasks before trusting it, and keep mutating operations behind the guard.

name: Digest Records For A Need
description: A need over a large body of the person's records reaches the planner as a few cited findings.
purpose: Lets a step that needs something from hundreds of records read all of them without a prompt that holds them, so cost and prompt size stay bounded and every finding can be traced to a record the person can open.
approach: One cheap-tier sub-analysis per window of one source group returns the findings that bear on the need with the ids they rest on; an id not in the window is dropped in code; the reduce step is code; digests are cached under the need, the background and the window's content.

measures_of_success: The ids cited are the ones the need rests on, no prompt passes its cap, an unchanged group costs nothing the second time, and a group that cannot be read is reported without failing the call.
parameters: Window, record and finding sizes, the number of sub-analyses per call and the concurrency, each overridable by name in meta.

outputs: The cited findings, the ids they rest on with their titles, and the status of every group.
effects: Model calls on the fast tier only for groups not already cached; reads only otherwise.

name: Index By Meaning
description: A card is found by what it means, however the question is worded.
purpose: Helps a person or a run find the card or note they need by meaning, including when they ask in different words.
approach: Embeds each item and ranks stored items by how close their meaning is to the question.
out_of_scope: Looking up an exact identifier or literal string, which needs keyword or content search, keeping the record of the cards it indexes (persist-cards does that) and choosing which cards a request reads (context-retriever does that).
milestones: 1. The labelled card is among the first three results for most questions, and median and tail query latency stay under the interactive caps at a fixed corpus size, measured against a Qdrant server.
knowledge: Embedding only the start of a long item loses facts near its end, an incident pinned by a failing case. Latency of an embedded local store is not the latency of a networked server, and the local embedder is smaller than the deployed one. Multi-tenant isolation by payload filter is preferred over a collection per tenant.
measures_of_success: The labelled card is among the first few results for most questions, mostly paraphrases, and median and tail latency stay under the interactive caps at the stated corpus size.
parameters: Collection prefix, storage path or server url, embedder and vector size, and per-call scope and number of results.
inputs: A query string and optional scope for search; item dictionaries with id, text, payload and fingerprint for upsert and sync.
outputs: Ranked hits with id, score, text and payload for search; counts for sync and count; the number deleted for eviction.
effects: Writes embedded points to the collection and re-embeds only items whose fingerprint changed; never raises, returning empty or zero on error.
usage_notes: Call sync on every run to keep the index fresh, pass a scope so private points stay private, and treat unscoped points as shared. Add a second store by implementing the protocol.
verdict_detail: memory_cosine is exactly equal to qdrant_embedded on the metric (memory_cosine 0.941 against qdrant_embedded 0.941), so qdrant_embedded stays

name: Spec Selection
description: The few specification records a request concerns are the ones in view.
purpose: Choose, from an ESOI specification index, the few records a new request concerns and their linked records, so the work starts from the intent that applies.
approach: Select the records an input concerns from a specification index, and return none when no record concerns it.
out_of_scope: Building the specification index, reading the chosen records in full, and ranking context cards (context-retriever does that).
milestones: 1. Labelled requests passed by the gated lexical and vector arm: 76 of 76, with every expected record present and no more than the ceiling returned.
knowledge: The ESOI specification index (version 1 JSON: entries, weighted terms, document frequencies); TF-IDF and reciprocal rank fusion; parallel batched LLM selection as in the card filter.
measures_of_success: On labelled inputs every expected record is selected; a failed vector or model call never removes a candidate; calls equal batches. Standing conditions: The records an input concerns are selected from the whole tree in one model call's latency, with no invented ids and no loss when a call fails.
parameters: k_lexical, k_vector, batch_size, max_workers, expand, model.
inputs: The request text, the loaded index, an optional model provider, an optional vector search callable returning entry ids.
outputs: A SpecSelection: ids best first then linked ids, the candidates shown to the model, which source proposed each, the number of calls and failed batches.
effects: One cheap model call per batch of candidates; none without a provider.
usage_notes: Load the index with load_spec_index (write it with `esoi spec index --out FILE`; its digest says when it is stale), pass the run's provider and the consumer's own vector search over the same entries, then read in full only the returned ids.
verdict_detail: lexical_vector_gated leads lexical_only (lexical_only 0.788 against lexical_vector_gated 0.903; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.203, 50 of 76 cases disagree); lexical_vector_gated leads lexical_vector (lexical_vector 0.816 against lexical_vector_gated 0.903; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.0888, 49 of 76 cases disagree; one of 2 looks, alpha 0.025); best guess, not yet significant: lexical_vector_llm 0.486 against lexical_vector_gated 0.903 on the point estimate; no case counts or per-case rows allow a test; lexical_vector_gated is better than solutions_and_problems_with_links (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=4.42e-05, 51 of 76 cases disagree)

name: Search Cards And Specs
description: One search shows the cards and specification records a run concerns.
purpose: Help each run see the cards and specification records it concerns in one ranked set, and see when no solution covers its request yet.
approach: Select a run's cards and specification records from one combined search, labelled by kind and by source.
out_of_scope: Drafting the wording of a new solution, which a run does when this search reports that none covers the request (esoi-application does that); its arms use spec-selection for records and context-retriever for cards.
milestones: 1. A combined labelled case set exists, with requests whose right answer mixes cards and records, requests with no solution yet, and requests that match only an ideal or a metric. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The merged pipeline scores at or above the recorded spec_selection balanced score and context_selection pass rate on their own cases, and ahead of the two separate pipelines on the mixed cases.
knowledge: How the two pipelines differ today, stage by stage. Candidates: cards from the card repository; records from the ESOI spec index, rebuilt when a record file changes. Lexical: IDF over a card's name, keywords, summary, terms, symbols and content (adapters/context_store_assembly.py), against field-weighted TF-IDF over the index's own terms (core/spec_selection.py). Vector: the card vector store or the Quest backend's search, against an injected local embedder over record lines (core/repo_specs.py). Fusion: weighted reciprocal-rank fusion with keyword above vector (select_context/hybrid_context_assembler.py), against plain reciprocal-rank fusion. Choice: a balanced-tier filter and a consolidation pass (core/card_filter.py), against a confidence gate that calls a model only for an unclear case. Output: a card result carries no kind, a record result does. Wiring: cards are assembled at the start of every run (core/orchestrator_run_begin.py); records only through tools (core/tools_repo_specs.py) or the deep-goal slice (core/spec_slice.py). A mounted store is read in place and never copied; the same principle holds for records. Context a run needs that is not a solution, read against the evolvable-structure skill: ideals decide what better means ("there are one or more ideals defined for every solution, and a practical metric to compare how well each implementation achieves the relevant ideals"), so a run choosing among alternatives or writing a new solution needs them; metrics are how a change is judged ("alternative implementations are compared via metrics"); an intent's vision statement settles which way to go when a request is ambiguous; problems are the entry point when nothing is built yet ("all solutions are motivated by a defined problem"). Reached by link in the working default: a solution brings its ideals, its metrics and its intent's frame; a problem brings its ideals and its intent. Not reached: a request whose words match only an ideal or a metric, when neither the linked problem nor the linked solution matches it; an intent whose folder holds no problem or solution. Folding the names of a solution's ideals and metric into its searchable text, as a card folds in its keywords, is the planned remedy, unmeasured. Tags (esoi/tags.csv) are a cheap filter or boost for the same search, planned and unmeasured.
measures_of_success: On the mixed cases the expected cards and records are in view under one budget; a request with no solution yet returns its problem or intent with "no solution yet"; on each half neither existing metric drops; an assembly makes one model call or none. Standing conditions: Never copy a record into a card store. Label every result with its kind and its source.
parameters: Candidate pool size per source, fusion weights per source and kind, the gate thresholds, which record kinds are ranked directly and which are reached through links, whether tags filter or boost, the shared character budget, and the assembly deadline.
inputs: The task text and run metadata (scope tags, deadline), the card repository and vector store, and the ESOI spec index of the repository root when one is found.
outputs: One assembled context: ranked items, each with its kind (card, or a record kind), source and id, the linked records each brings, a "no solution yet" mark on a problem or intent that no solution serves, the rendered view under one budget, and the sources for the answer's explanation.
effects: Reads cards and records and writes neither; at most one cheap model call, none for a clear or an empty case.
usage_notes: Built: solutions_and_problems_with_links (core/unified_search.py, with adapters/card_views.py for a card store) answers the read-only tool search_cards_and_specs beside find_specs. A run's context is still assembled by the two pipelines side by side (two_pipelines), and what is selected follows the metric: on 2026-10-22 the merged arm led the mixed cases but held neither half against the best free arm on its own cases (spec_selection, context_selection; numbers in the results log), so two_pipelines stays selected. every_record_a_view stays recorded as the alternative and is not built. A "no solution yet" result is the trigger for the run to define a solution, recorded through track-runs-on-records.

name: Write Through MCP
description: A write to an outside tool server happens only when it is allowed.
purpose: Carry out one named change on an external tool server, and only when an explicit allowlist permits that operation.
approach: Permit a write to an external tool server only when it is on the write allowlist, and run it once with the exact arguments given.
out_of_scope: Reads from a tool server (quest-context does that), any operation that is not on the write allowlist, and deciding which quest change a request asks for (quest-change-executor does that).
milestones: 1. Allowlist cases passed by the write adapter: 15 of 15, with every refused operation making zero server calls. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. Allowed writes run once with exact arguments on a live MCP server, recorded on the same cases.
knowledge: A write allowlist is separate from any read allowlist, so being readable grants nothing here. A refused operation must never touch the server. Names are alias-prefixed so servers do not collide, and the planner may pass the prefixed or bare form. Real servers are not exercised in the offline arm.
measures_of_success: An allowed call reaches the client once with exact arguments, a disallowed call makes zero server calls, and server errors and dead connections come back as failed results with details recorded. Standing conditions: Guarantee that exactly the requested mutation runs once, and that anything off the allowlist is refused with no server call. Make every attempt auditable.
parameters: Server alias and connection spec, the write allowlist of tool names, and the timeout.
inputs: An operation name (prefixed or bare) and its arguments; a discovery call for the writable catalogue.
outputs: A write result with success, error and an audit detail of the tool, arguments and whether it executed; a list of writable operations with schemas.
effects: One mutating call on the external server when allowed; no effect when refused.
usage_notes: List writable operations first, pick at most one, and escalate when refused or failed. Keep the write allowlist narrower than the read one.
verdict_detail: allowlist_writer is better than real_stdio_server (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.00781, 8 of 15 cases disagree)

name: Place On A Quest
description: Every message is served by the quest it is about.
purpose: Say which of the person's quests a message, goal, note or task belongs to, or none, the same way on every surface that picks one.
approach: Rank the person's quests for the text by what each quest holds (its words) and what it means (its embedding), both reading what the quest is for (its vision statement and purpose, one shared text) beside the owner's scope, which stays the binding routing rule, show the model the best candidates first by number, and let the model pick which are about the text, or none; the user's priority orders what is left. The host (the Quest backend) owns the quests and supplies the function; the runner calls it through this port and never guesses a quest by its own heuristics when it is present.
out_of_scope: Holding the quests and their intents as the standing view and framing work with them (Quest Intents). A quest the person chose explicitly, such as the Quest chat of one quest: an explicit choice is not classification, so the pin stays. Whether a write may bind to a quest unasked, which is the host's write guard over the placement.
milestones: 1. Placement is scored on labelled messages over an account of many quests, none included, and on real labelled messages where a machine holds them.
knowledge: The model alone, shown a long list of quests, reads only the first of them and picks by topic words; embeddings of a quest's title do not see its milestones, and a cue like 'get the store release moving' is only resolved by them; 'none' is a right answer that a ranker with no model never gives.
measures_of_success: The share of labelled messages placed on exactly the labelled quests (none included), balanced with cost and time, on public invented cases and on real labelled ones.
parameters: The person's quests (title, vision statement, purpose, category, state, scope, open outcomes), the previous message, the quest the person is working in (home) and how many quests a text may be placed on.
inputs: A message, the previous message and the person's quests.
outputs: The quests the message is about (empty when none fits) and every quest ranked best first.
effects: One model call per message; reads the person's quests.
usage_notes: Every surface that picks a quest from text calls the host function: the daily plan, reflection notes, insights, the AI task form, chat task pickup, task delegation and the runner's own turns. When the answer is none, ask one short question rather than guess.
